chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Acting versus singing, showmanship and projection without a microphone
summary: The techniques differ; theater work needs projection and playing with the audience, and the show was a musical comedy.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Alright I guess I just have one question to ask about this last of your acting experiences. You were not without experience before. You talked about the other stage appearances you made. But do you - what comments would you have to make about the difference between acting, straight acting in the kind of play you were just in and jazz singing or popular singing?

Well, there's a difference alright, the difference being the technique of projecting. Of course in 'My Old Friends' and of course now, they are using microphones more on stage than they used to. But, the real died-in-the-wool-actors, they abhor the use of microphones on the legitimate stage. And of course, there are millions of applications on stage. I mean, even without microphones in sight there's microphones in the stage, you know, in the curtains up above out of sight. Of course, I used the mike in the production but I used the mike because the scene was supposed to be part of a party that was being held in the center and they would have a microphone there. So I think I would have needed it really. I don't think that I could project
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

in a theatre without the benefit of a microphone. There are some people, actors, I mean real actors - I do not consider myself a real actress. I'm a singer mainly. The acting from a standpoint of what I had to do came alright. And I projected alright, my lines. But whether I could have projected the singing voice remains to be seen. I don't think I could. So acting not being my main career I'm not frustrated if I don't get called for parts in a theatre because I don't know whether I could handle them or not. The main thing about singing in a theatre is projecting and that's another technique altogether. I can sing without a microphone, of course, in a small room. I've done it, but in a theatre you got to think twice about that. And you would have to change your approach. You really have to sing out and you have to almost shout your song unless you have that deep voice. And I don't think I could do it. That would have an affect on my singing style from the way I sing in a club. Of course, that was a good experience for me. I'm a little looser now when I sing in a club because now I'm an actress. I say a few things before where I used to just sing one song after the other. Now I make a few
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
comments. You know, I play around with the audience a little bit. I got to show off my acting ability. So that . . .
The kind of showmanship you were talking about earlier, you say is so necessary if you want to entertain people. That's also part of singing anyway. It's kind of a theatrical dimension.

My, the show itself was a musical comedy in a way. And my particular part in it was funny, you know. So I guess acting to me, I've always wanted to be a little bit on the comedienne side. So now I can do it and get by with it. Otherwise, you know, what is she trying to prove. But now that I've become an Actress I can get by with telling a few jokes and things like that, or make a few comments hoping that I'll get a laugh. And every little bit helps.
